summary: Backend-only verification of weather-autofill concurrency hardening + observability. Added /app/backend/tests/test_weather_autofill_concurrency.py with 14 pytest cases covering: (a) structured logger.warning for all 4 failure categories (TIMEOUT / CONNECTION_ERROR / HTTP_5xx / OTHER) in BOTH _geocode and _fetch_weather via caplog + monkeypatched requests.get [8 tests], (b) 5-min freshness cache — cold call populates DR, next 3 calls skip Open-Meteo entirely (call counter unchanged), (c) coalescing — 50 concurrent POSTs to the same (tenant, project, date) collapse to <=3 outbound requests.get invocations, (d) semaphore(20) cap — 30 concurrent POSTs to 30 different coalesce keys (varied report_date) with 250ms fake latency; peak in-flight outbound observed = 20 (exact match) and never exceeds cap; some concurrency observed (>=2), (e) negative cache — 60s TTL on _fetch_weather None result, 2nd/3rd calls skip requests.get, (f) all-4xx contract — monkeypatched requests.get raising ConnectionError returns 422 JSON with detail < 200 chars, (g) regression — real Kansas City / MO happy path returns 200 with weather fields populated. Also fixed iteration_14's regression suite (test_weather_autofill_no_5xx.py) which had begun failing after the freshness-cache feature was added: 4 monkeypatch tests were short-circuited because the DR still had fresh weather_fetched_at from the happy-path test; added _clear_dr_weather() helper + autouse cache-reset fixture. Combined run: 23/23 pass in ~27s.
critical_code_review_comments: Semaphore + coalesce-lock init is lazy inside the endpoint (`if _wx_outbound_sem is None: ... = _asyncio.Semaphore(20)`). Two simultaneous cold requests could each pass the None check before either assigns — a benign race that would create two semaphores momentarily, dropping the effective cap for the first burst. Cheap fix: initialise both at module import inside a startup event, or wrap the None-check in `_wx_coalesce_locks_mutex` (but that itself is lazy). Not a P0 since the semaphore only guards the outbound-call section and process boot is single-request in practice, but worth flagging.

`_wx_outbound_sem` is bound to whichever event loop first hits the endpoint. In a multi-loop server (uvicorn workers = independent processes so OK, but pytest-asyncio uses one loop per test) an asyncio.Semaphore created on a different loop will raise `got Future attached to a different loop`. Our tests dodge this by keeping one asgi_client fixture per test, but if the semaphore is created inside a background task on an alternate loop it would blow up. Consider `asyncio.Semaphore(20)` created inside the request (per-loop cache) rather than a module-level singleton.

daily_reports_router.py is 2361 lines — still exceeds the 700-line guideline. The 330-line 'Weather auto-fill' block (lines 1510-1839) is now large enough and self-contained enough to live in its own /app/backend/services/weather_autofill.py module; would also let logging tests target its own module logger namespace.

In-memory caches (_GEOCODE_CACHE, _WEATHER_CACHE, _wx_coalesce_locks) are per-pod. Under horizontal scaling each pod caches independently, so with N pods you get up to N outbound calls per unique (project, date) instead of 1. Fine for 100+ concurrent DR opens on a single pod (as spec'd) but call it out for the roadmap if we ever go multi-pod behind a load balancer — a shared Redis TTL cache would fix it.

Freshness check is 5 min but weather cache is 30 min — mismatch means the endpoint's 'return cached DR' path is stricter than the underlying weather cache. Not a bug but an operator surprise: forcing a Refresh 6-29 min after the last fetch will hit the OUTBOUND semaphore path just to get a value that _fetch_weather then serves from its own in-memory cache anyway. Consider aligning to a single TTL constant.
test_credentials: Ephemeral registration per run: wxconc+<timestamp>@example.com / TestPass123! via /api/auth/register. Cleaned up in module-scope teardown fixture (drops tenant docs across daily_reports, projects, users, tenants, daily_presence, audit_logs).
seed_data_creation: One tenant + 1 KC/MO project + 31 DRs (1 for freshness/coalescing on today, 30 for semaphore test on staggered past dates). All wiped in teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: `cd /app/backend && REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<url> pytest tests/test_weather_autofill_concurrency.py tests/test_weather_autofill_no_5xx.py -o asyncio_mode=auto`. The concurrency file loads /app/backend/.env via python-dotenv so JWT_SECRET matches the running backend (else 401s). Both files share the ASGI-in-process transport pattern; if you add more monkeypatched endpoint tests, remember to _clear_dr_weather() so the 5-min freshness cache doesn't short-circuit the monkeypatched _geocode/_fetch_weather. Peak in-flight outbound observed in semaphore test was exactly 20 with 30 concurrent inputs & 250ms fake latency — that's the sweet spot; if you raise fake latency, raise concurrency proportionally.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bug found. Verification only. All 7 requested checks pass: (1) 4 exception categories logged in both helpers, (2) freshness cache returns 200 with 0 extra outbound calls, (3) coalescing collapses 50 same-key hits to <=3 outbound (typically exactly 2: 1 geocode + 1 weather from the winning request), (4) semaphore cap holds at 20 under 30-way parallelism, (5) negative cache holds for 60s, (6) ConnectionError → 422 JSON < 200 chars, (7) real KC/MO happy path returns 200 with all weather fields populated.
